tldr: The actual normalized IPW marginal-median contrast has a uniformly valid shared-record marked-Poisson crossing law on the entire fixed class \(\mathcal M\), despite positive marginal density. The same rare records generate its baseline and random local rank increments; the proved fixed-sample coupling preserves the original sample and its complement. A positive-probability discrepancy from inversion of the same empirical score establishes that the anchor\textquotesingle s conditional small-ball premise cannot simply be replaced by positive marginal density. Original-record refitted subsamples consistently calibrate the law without supplied outcome nuisances and yield total connected intervals with asymptotic coverage \(.90\), uniformly exact expected-length order \(n^{-1/3}\), and positive limiting width constants. Finite spatial and observable sampling-law certificates quantify truncation, inverse perturbation, and Monte Carlo error.
gap: The fixed-quantile IPW anchor controls local remainders through its ordinary-supremum conditional small-ball condition (11). Positive marginal density does not imply this condition. The benchmark also lies outside the named differentiable-score and finite-weight-variance comparator premises.
fill: Joint shared-record crossing theory, the same-score discrepancy, model-specific calibration and dependent inverse certificates form the contribution. The diffuse reduction and generic Poisson argmin and subsampling mechanisms receive no novelty credit. Avella-Medina--Davis--Samorodnitsky Section 7 includes an IPW QTT analysis of NSW--PSID post-intervention earnings \cite{AvellaMedinaDavisSamorodnitsky2025}. Its accompanying marginal-QTE illustration in Figure 7 supplies the shared treated weighted-quantile ingredient whose weak-overlap calibration can be sensitive to conditional outcome collapse. The QTT calculation in Figure 8 instead uses an unweighted treated quantile and an odds-weighted counterfactual control quantile. The marginal-QTE benchmark addresses that shared calibration mechanism; it does not equate its causal contrast with the full published QTT estimand. Membership of the published data in the benchmark and a numerical reanalysis are not asserted.
